You are building an admin product catalog page for an e-commerce team.

The catalog is read-heavy and should feel fast for day-to-day browsing, so avoid re-querying product data on every request.

Admins can trigger a "Sync latest catalog" action from the page when upstream ERP/PIM data changes (pricing, inventory, availability). After submitting, they should be able to continue working immediately, even if the product list is briefly stale.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.
I'll inspect the Next.js app and caching docs first so the catalog page can stay cached and the sync action invalidates `"products"` without blocking the admin.

9  	`revalidateTag` allows you to invalidate cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag.
10 	
11 	This function is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. With the recommended `max` profile, users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background.

18 	
19 	### Revalidation Behavior
20 	
21 	Calling `revalidateTag` marks the tagged data as stale. The next request for that data kicks off a revalidation and is served stale content while it runs, using stale-while-revalidate semantics. The second argument sets how long stale content may be served. Past that, a request blocks until the revalidation completes.
22

5  	
6  	`updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).
7  	
8  	This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.
9  	
10 	## Usage
11 	
12 	`updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.
13 	
14 	If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.
15 	
16 	> **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.
17 	
18 	## Parameters
19 	
20 	```tsx
21 	updateTag(tag: string): void;
22 	```
23 	
24 	- `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to update. Must not exceed 256 characters. This value is case-sensitive.
25 	
26 	Tags must first be assigned to cached data. You can do this in two ways:
27 	
28 	- Using the [`next.tags`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) option with `fetch` for caching external API requests:

40 	  'use cache'

42 	  // ...
43 	}
44 	```

53 	
54 	- **`updateTag`**:
55 	  - Can only be used in Server Actions

3  	description: API Reference for the unstable_cache function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	> **Note:**
7  	> This API has been replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) in Next.js 16.
8  	> We recommend opting into [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and replacing `unstable_cache` with the `use cache` directive.
9  	
10 	`unstable_cache` allows you to cache the results of expensive operations, like database queries, and reuse them across multiple requests.
11 	
12 	```jsx
13 	import { getUser } from './data';
14 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache';
15 	
16 	const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
17 	  async (id) => getUser(id),
18 	  ['my-app-user']
19 	);
20 	
21 	export default async function Component({ userID }) {
22 	  const user = await getCachedUser(userID);
23 	  ...
24 	}
25 	```
26 	
27 	> **Good to know**:
28 	>
29 	> - Accessing request data such as `headers` or `cookies` inside a cache scope is not supported. Read the data outside the cached function and pass the values you need as arguments.
30 	> - This API uses Next.js' built-in cache to persist the result across requests and deployments. See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
31 	
32 	## Unsupported operations
33 	
34 	The function passed to `unstable_cache` cannot depend on the incoming request. Read values from `cookies()` or `headers()` before calling the cached function, then pass those values as arguments so they become part of the cache key.
35 	
36 	The cached function also cannot:
37 	
38 	- Call `connection()`, which requires an incoming request
39 	- Enable or disable draft mode
40 	- Call `revalidateTag()`, `updateTag()`, or `revalidatePath()` during cache execution
41 	- Call a function that uses the `use cache: private` directive
42 	
43 	Perform request-dependent work before calling the cached function. Perform mutations and revalidation afterward from a Server Action or Route Handler.
44 	
45 	## Parameters
46 	
47 	```jsx
48 	const data = unstable_cache(fetchData, keyParts, options)()
49 	```
50 	
51 	- `fetchData`: This is an asynchronous function that fetches the data you want to cache. It must be a function that returns a `Promise`.
52 	- `keyParts`: This is an extra array of keys that further adds identification to the cache. By default, `unstable_cache` already uses the arguments and the stringified version of your function as the cache key. It is optional in most cases; the only time you need to use it is when you use external variables without passing them as parameters. However, it is important to add closures used within the function if you do not pass them as parameters.
53 	- `options`: This is an object that controls how the cache behaves. It can contain the following properties:
54 	  - `tags`: An array of tags that can be used to control cache invalidation. Next.js will not use this to uniquely identify the function.
55 	  - `revalidate`: The number of seconds after which the cache should be revalidated. Omit or pass `false` to cache indefinitely or until matching `revalidateTag()` or `revalidatePath()` methods are called.
56 	
57 	## Returns
58 	
59 	`unstable_cache` returns a function that when invoked, returns a Promise that resolves to the cached data. If the data is not in the cache, the provided function will be invoked, and its result will be cached and returned.
60 	
61 	## Example
62 	
63 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
64 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
65 	
66 	export default async function Page({
67 	  params,
68 	}: {
69 	  params: Promise<{ userId: string }>
70 	}) {
71 	  const { userId } = await params
72 	  const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
73 	    async () => {
74 	      return { id: userId }
75 	    },
76 	    [userId], // add the user ID to the cache key
77 	    {
78 	      tags: ['users'],
79 	      revalidate: 60,
80 	    }
81 	  )
82 	
83 	  //...
84 	}
85 	```

93 	    async () => {

95 	    },
96 	    [userId], // add the user ID to the cache key
97 	    {

15 	> This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. 16 	
17 	Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:
18 	
19 	- **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
20 	- **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).
21 	
22 	## `cacheLife`
23 	
24 	[`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
25 	
26 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
27 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
28 	
29 	export async function getProducts() {
30 	  'use cache'
31 	  cacheLife('hours')
32 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	`cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:
37 	
38 	| Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
39 	| --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
40 	| `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |
41 	| `seconds` | 30s     | 1s           | 60s      |
42 	| `minutes` | 5m      | 1m           | 1h       |
43 	| `hours`   | 5m      | 1h           | 1d       |
44 	| `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
45 	| `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
46 	| `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |
47 	
48 	For fine-grained control, pass an object:
49 	
50 	```tsx highlight={2-6}
51 	'use cache'
52 	cacheLife({
53 	  stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
54 	  revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
55 	  expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
56 	})
57 	```
58 	
59 	> **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.
60 	
61 	See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.
62 	
63 	## `cacheTag`
64 	
65 	[`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope:
66 	
67 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
68 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
69 	
70 	export async function getProducts() {
71 	  'use cache'
72 	  cacheTag('products')
73 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
74 	}
75 	```
76 	
77 	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
78 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
79 	
80 	export async function getProducts() {
81 	  'use cache'
82 	  cacheTag('products')
83 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
84 	}
85 	```
86 	
87 	Once tagged, invalidate the cache using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) or [`updateTag`](#updatetag).
88 	
89 	See the [`cacheTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) to learn more.
90 	
91 	## `revalidateTag`
92 	
93 	`revalidateTag` invalidates cache entries by tag using stale-while-revalidate semantics — stale content is served immediately while fresh content loads in the background. This is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, like blog posts or product catalogs.
94 	
95 	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
96 	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
97 	
98 	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
99 	  // Mutate data
100	  revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
101	}
102	```
103	
104	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
105	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
106	
107	export async function updateUser(id) {
108	  // Mutate data
109	  revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
110	}
111	```
112	
113	You can reuse the same tag in multiple functions to revalidate them all at once. Call `revalidateTag` in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
114	
115	> **Good to know:** The second argument sets how long stale content can be served while fresh content generates in the background. Once it expires, subsequent requests block until fresh content is ready. Using `'max'` gives the longest stale window.
116	
117	See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more.
118	
119	## `updateTag`
120	
121	`updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/guides/server-actions).
122	
123	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher
124	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
125	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
126	
127	export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
128	  const post = await db.post.create({
129	    data: {
130	      title: formData.get('title'),
131	      content: formData.get('content'),
132	    },
133	  })
134	
135	  updateTag('posts')
136	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
137	}
138	```
139	
140	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher
141	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
142	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
143	
144	export async function createPost(formData) {
145	  const post = await db.post.create({
146	    data: {
147	      title: formData.get('title'),
148	      content: formData.get('content'),
149	    },
150	  })
151	
152	  updateTag('posts')
153	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
154	}
155	```
156	
157	|              | `updateTag`                                   | `revalidateTag`                      |
158	| ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
159	| **Where**    | Server Actions only                           | Server Actions and Route Handlers    |
160	| **Behavior** | Immediately expires cache                     | Stale-while-revalidate               |
161	| **Use case** | Read-your-own-writes (user sees their change) | Background refresh (slight delay OK) |
162	
163	See the [`updateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) to learn more.
164	
165	## `revalidatePath`
166	
167	`revalidatePath` invalidates all cached data for a specific route path. Use it when you want to revalidate a route without knowing which tags are associated with it.
168	
169	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
170	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
171	
172	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
173	  // Mutate data
174	  revalidatePath('/profile')
175	}
176	```
177	
178	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
179	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
180	
181	export async function updateUser(id) {
182	  // Mutate data
183	  revalidatePath('/profile')
184	}
185	```
186	
187	> **Good to know**: Prefer tag-based revalidation (`revalidateTag`/`updateTag`) over path-based when possible — it's more precise and avoids over-invalidating.
188	
189	See the [`revalidatePath` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) to learn more.
190	
191	## What should I cache?
192	
193	Cache data that doesn't depend on [runtime data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#working-with-runtime-apis) and that you're OK serving from cache for a period of time. Use `use cache` with `cacheLife` to describe that behavior.
194	
195	When content doesn't need time-based revalidation, for example data from a CMS, use [`cacheTag`](#cachetag) and a long [`cacheLife`](#cachelife) like `max` to keep it in the static shell. Configure the content source to trigger a webhook, or other notification, that calls [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) when the content changes. This reduces unnecessary time-based revalidation for content that hasn't changed.
196	
197	> **Good to know:** In serverless environments, in-memory cache entries may not persist across revalidations. See [runtime caching considerations](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations) for details.
